runs.t: AI can accelerate test-case discovery, fixture creation and failure analysis, but generated tests still need an independent behavioral oracle. The goal is finding faults, not merely increasing test count.

Derive tests from requirements and threat models, ask AI for edge cases and properties, then inspect assertions and run tests against deliberate mutants. Verify fixtures do not silently bypass authorization or concurrency.
An AI assistant might generate tests for overlapping booking intervals, leap days, cancellations and two users racing for the last room. The expected outcomes must be confirmed by the business rules.
AI often writes tests that assert the current implementation instead of the intended behavior. High coverage with incorrect assertions can create false confidence and lock in bugs.

Ask an agent to derive reservation tests solely from a written policy, then compare them with implementation and flag mismatches instead of adjusting expectations to pass.
Review criteria:

items.t: State the expected behavior and at least one failure or edge case before asking an agent to implement anything.
Inspect the boundary conditions and dependency direction, not only the happy-path result.
Demand observable evidence: tests, measured results, or a justified design decision.
